lead_in: On the memorial of Mary’s Presentation: the Catholic Encyclopedia on the apocryphal account and the feast’s origin.

excerpt.text: The Protoevangel of James, the Gospel of Pseudo-Matthew, the Gospel of the Nativity of Mary, and other apocryphal writings (Walker, “Apocryph. Gosp.”, Edinburgh, 1873) relate that Mary, at the age of three, was brought by her parents to the Temple, in fulfillment of a vow, there to be educated. The corresponding feast originated in the Orient, probably in Syria, the home of the apocrypha.
excerpt.attribution: Catholic Encyclopedia (1911), “Feast of the Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary”
